text: Offeror must meet Limitations on Subcontracting (LOS) requirements and comply with applicable VAAR subpart 819.70 and SBA regulations.

citations.quote: Offeror must be certified/verified as an SD/VOSB in the SBA SBS VIP (Veteran Information Pages) VetCert as an SD/VOSB.
Offeror must meet LOS (Limitations on Subcontracting) requirements and per the LOS listed clauses below.
Compliance with the LOS clauses must be asserted by the offeror in the email accompanying their quote.

When awarded a contract action, including orders under multiple-award contracts, an SDVOSB agrees that in the performance of the contract, the SDVOSB shall comply with requirements in VAAR subpart 819.70 and SBA regulations on small business size and government contracting programs at 13 CFR part 121 and part 125, including the non-manufacturer rule and limitations on subcontracting requirements in 13 CFR 121.406(b) and 13 CFR 125.6.

For the purpose of limitations on subcontracting, only VIP-listed SDVOSBs (including independent contractors) shall be considered eligible and/or “similarly situated” (i.e., a firm that has the same small business program status as the prime contractor).
An SDVOSB must meet the NAICS size standard assigned by the prime contractor and be listed in VIP to count as similarly situated.
Any work that a first tier VIP-listed SDVOSB subcontractor further subcontracts will count towards the percent of subcontract amount that cannot be exceeded.
For supply or construction contracts, the cost of materials is excluded and not considered to be subcontracted.

When a contract includes both services and supplies, the 50 percent limitation shall apply only to the portion of the contract with the preponderance of the expenditure upon which the assigned NAICS is based.
An SDVOSB shall comply with the limitations on subcontracting as follows:
A VOSB must meet the NAICS size standard assigned by the prime contractor and be listed in VIP to count as similarly situated.
Any work that a first tier VIP-listed VOSB subcontractor further subcontracts will count towards the percent of subcontract amount that cannot be exceeded.
For supply or construction contracts, the cost of materials is excluded and not considered to be subcontracted.

When a contract includes both services and supplies, the 50 percent limitation shall apply only to the portion of the contract with the preponderance of the expenditure upon which the assigned NAICS is based.
A VOSB shall comply with the limitations on subcontracting as follows: [Contracting Officer check as appropriate.] __By the end of the performance period for each order issued under the contract.
